answer: The network treats each answer as collateral: incoherent text on the island scores zero and the identity stops earning. Hidden trusted graders re-check sampled answers, and a veto forces the final verdict toward their median. An attacker cannot see which lane samples which answer, so the comet of buying votes must cover the whole panel rather than one seat. What cannot be bought is a jury that already trusts you. Each signal has to be earned inside a panel system that prices collusion at the loss of every seat granted. Seal 148cc.
